Work in the git worktree at /opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform (branch feature/staff-platform, checked out from the Nxeon production repo at /opt/nxeon — do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging directly, only this worktree). Node modules are already installed there (a real `npm install`, not a symlink).

This worktree already has Phase 1 (schema) and Phase 2 (RBAC gating primitive) of a larger staff-platform feature landed and fully verified (tsc clean, all relevant tests pass). Read the full plan first: /root/.claude/plans/validated-napping-possum.md — it has the complete context (why this exists, all 7 phases, the exact ground truth about the codebase). Also read `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/lib/staff-grants.ts` (already built) and `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/lib/rbac.ts` (already extended) in full — these are your foundation.

## Your job: Phase 3 — Admin "Staff" management UI

The owner just hired their first employee and needs a way to: create employee accounts, hand-pick exactly which tools each one can access (not fixed roles — a checklist of individual grants), configure a per-employee IP whitelist, and jump to that employee's activity log. This must be reachable ONLY by the real ADMIN role, forever — never delegable to other staff, since it's the tool that GRANTS access to everything else.

Read `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/app/admin/staff/page.tsx` and `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/lib/actions-staff.ts` (the existing simple role-promotion page) in full first — you're extending this, not replacing it wholesale. Also read `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/app/admin/users/page.tsx` + `/opt/nxeon-wip-staff-platform/app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` for the established list+detail split pattern to mirror (list page links to a per-user detail page).

Build:
1. Extend `app/admin/staff/page.tsx` into a list of ALL staff (SUPPORT/BILLING/ADMIN/EMPLOYEE), each linking to a new `app/admin/staff/[id]/page.tsx` detail page. Both stay gated `requireArea("platform")` (import from `@/lib/rbac`, NOT the new `staff-grants` module — staff management itself is never grantable, only ADMIN reaches it, exactly like today).
2. On the detail page (or inline for the list, your call on UX, but a detail page per employee is cleaner given how much goes on one): a **grant checklist** — one checkbox per entry in `GRANTABLE_AREAS` (already exported from `lib/staff-grants.ts` — read it, don't invent your own list). New actions in `lib/actions-staff.ts`: `setStaffGrant(userId: string, area: Area, granted: boolean)` (upsert/delete a `StaffGrant` row via `db.staffGrant`), each `requireAdmin()`-gated (import from `@/lib/auth`) — never `requireGrant`, since granting grants must always be ADMIN-only. Also `createEmployee(email: string, name: string): Promise<{ok:true,tempPassword:string}|{ok:false,error:string}>` — creates a `Role.EMPLOYEE` user with a securely-generated temp password (look at how `prisma/seed.ts` or `lib/actions-staff.ts`'s existing user-creation-adjacent code hashes passwords — likely bcrypt, check `lib/auth.ts` for the exact hashing call used at login/register so you use the identical function, not a different one).
3. **IP whitelist config** — add/remove-row UI on the same detail page. New actions `addStaffIp(userId: string, cidr: string, label?: string)` / `removeStaffIp(userId: string, id: string)`, `requireAdmin()`-gated, validating the CIDR through `normalizeCidr` from `lib/firewall-rules.ts` (read that file first — it's already there, reuse it, don't reimplement CIDR validation) before writing to `db.staffIpAllow`. Show existing `StaffIpAllow` rows with a delete button per row.
4. **Per-employee activity link** — a link/button on the detail page to `/admin/audit?staff=<userId>` (this filter doesn't exist yet — a parallel task is adding it to `/admin/audit`; just wire the link now, it'll work once that lands — don't build the filter yourself, that's out of scope for you).
5. **Quick-replies management** (`CannedReply` model, already in the schema) — a simple list+create+edit+delete UI. Your call whether this lives on `/admin/staff` itself or a small new `/admin/canned-replies` page (I'd lean toward a small separate page since it's conceptually unrelated to staff/grants — use your judgment). New file `lib/actions-canned-replies.ts`, actions gated with `requireAnyGrant(["supportTickets", "liveChat"])` from `lib/staff-grants.ts` (so a granted EMPLOYEE can create their own replies too, not just ADMIN) for read/create/edit, but keep delete `requireAdmin()`-gated if you think that's safer (your call — a support person deleting a snippet they didn't write is low-risk either way, so don't over-think this one).

New components: `components/admin/StaffGrantChecklist.tsx`, `components/admin/StaffIpAllowlist.tsx` (both client components, following whatever form/action pattern the existing `/admin/users` page or `/admin/staff` page already uses — check e.g. how `SuspendUserButton` or similar client components in `components/admin/` call a server action and handle pending/error state, and match that style rather than inventing a new one).

## Constraints
- Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (set `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/dummy"` as an env var for this and any Prisma-related command — there's no real database connected in this worktree, schema/type checking doesn't need one). Do NOT run `npm run build` or start any server — this worktree isn't deployed anywhere yet.
- Do not touch `app/staff/*` (a separate task is building the employee portal shell there) or `lib/actions-work.ts`/`components/work/*` (a separate task is building the task-management system) — stay in your lane: `app/admin/staff/**`, `lib/actions-staff.ts`, `lib/actions-canned-replies.ts` (new), `components/admin/StaffGrantChecklist.tsx` (new), `components/admin/StaffIpAllowlist.tsx` (new), and optionally a new `app/admin/canned-replies/page.tsx`.
- This is real production code (eventually promoted from staging) for a business that just hired someone — no placeholder/mock data, no TODO stubs. Every action must actually work end-to-end against the real Prisma models already in the schema.
- Follow the codebase's existing discipline: no comments explaining WHAT the code does; only comments for non-obvious WHY (this codebase's own style is dense with "why," read a few existing lib/actions-*.ts files to match the tone before writing your own).

## When done
Report: exact files created/modified, confirmation `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes cleanly (paste the exact command you ran with the DATABASE_URL env var), and a summary of every action you added with its exact gate (so a reviewer can spot-check that nothing is under-gated).

1	# Nxeon staff platform — roles, employee portal, and a project/task system
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Nxeon just hired its first employee (marketing + customer support). Today the codebase has no way to give one specific person a hand-picked subset of admin tools — access is all-or-nothing per role (`CUSTOMER | SUPPORT | BILLING | ADMIN`), and almost everything outside billing/fleet/support is bucketed into one ADMIN-only `"platform"` area (Reddit templates, the company inbox, mailboxes, settings, staff, audit log, and more all share that one gate). The owner wants: a dedicated portal for employees (separate from both the customer dashboard and the full `/admin` ops portal), the ability to hand-pick exactly which tools each individual employee can use, a per-employee IP whitelist, and a real internal project/task-management system ("a ClickUp alternative") usable by staff with full admin oversight of everything they do. This is production work (`/opt/nxeon`) — a mistake here risks over-exposing customer data to a new hire, so it's built additively, tested on staging, and verified with a real test employee account before every promotion to prod.
6	
7	For the first employee specifically, the owner wants: Support tickets, Live chat, the Reddit template library, the company Inbox, company Mailboxes, and a new limited (name/email/signup date/ticket count/server count only) Clients view — plus a snippet library for quick replies in tickets/chat, which doesn't exist today and is being added alongside.
8	
9	## Key decisions (confirmed with the owner)
10	
11	- **Separate, dedicated employee portal** (own nav/shell), not a permission-filtered view of `/admin`.
12	- **Per-employee custom grants**, not fixed named roles — the owner checks off exactly which tools each individual hire gets.
13	- **New minimal Clients view** for limited access — no financials, no IP/location history, no audit trail, no impersonate. Just name/email/signup date/ticket count/server count.
14	- **"Mailboxes" = company mailboxes** (admin@/support@-style), paired with the company Inbox — not customer email hosting.
15	- **Live chat + a quick-replies snippet library are in scope for this pass** (my recommendation, since they're core to a support hire's job); a knowledge-base/handbook view is an explicit fast-follow, not built now — needs a first look at the existing `kb.ts`/`kb-llm.ts`/`/admin/docs` code to see what's actually reusable before committing to an approach.
16	
17	## Ground truth confirmed this session (verified directly against the code, not just recalled)
18	
19	- `lib/rbac.ts`: `Area` union has exactly 8 values (`overview, analytics, clients, support, fleet, billing, accounting, platform`), a static `AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]>` map, `canAccess(role, area)`, `isStaff(role)` (`SUPPORT|BILLING|ADMIN`), `HREF_AREA` (route → area, defaults to `"platform"`), `requireArea(area)` (redirect-based page guard, `/login` if signed out, `/dashboard` if not staff, `/admin` if wrong area). Used at ~85 admin pages and ~30 action files, often re-checked per action as defense in depth.
20	- `platform` is a genuine ADMIN-only catch-all shared by 14+ unrelated action files (ads, agency, SEO, cold-email, broadcast, staff, audit, reddit, mail, mailboxes, …) — confirmed via grep. It must not be restructured wholesale; new narrow areas get carved out instead, leaving `platform`'s other ~25 routes untouched.
21	- `support` (the existing area) is shared by far more than the ticket queue: live chat (`lib/actions-chat.ts`, 12 confirmed `requireArea("support")` call sites), the Discord support bridge, feedback, two unread-count API routes, and a structural test (`test/discord-oauth-guards.test.ts`) that hardcodes the literal string `requireArea("support")`. Renaming/splitting `support` itself is out — new narrow areas (`supportTickets`, `liveChat`) are added alongside it instead, and only the ticket/chat call sites migrate to them.
22	- `lib/actions-support.ts:50-52` — confirmed by direct read: `requireTicketActor()` returns `{ id: user.id, isSupportStaff: canAccess(user.role, "support") }`, and this same helper is used for BOTH staff and customers viewing their own ticket (`ticketOwner.userId !== user.id && !user.isSupportStaff`). This is the single line that governs staff-vs-customer ticket permissions — one clean edit point.

/**
 * The single definition of "the same email address".
 *
 * `User.email` is `@unique` in Postgres, and a Postgres unique index is
 * CASE-SENSITIVE. Register and login stored and queried the address exactly as
 * it was typed, while `requestPasswordReset` lowercased it first. So a customer
 * who signed up as `Alice@Example.com` — which is what a phone keyboard produces
 * unless you fight it, because it auto-capitalises the first letter of a field —
 * had an account row no reset lookup could ever find. The reset form still
 * answered "If an account exists for that email, a reset link is on its way",
 * because that non-enumerating reply is correct and must stay. The result was a
 * customer locked out of their own account with no error, no email, and nothing
 * on screen suggesting anything had gone wrong.
 *
 * The fix is not "lowercase it in three more places" — that is the shape that
 * caused the bug, and the fourth place would drift too. Every write and every
 * lookup of a user's address goes through this one function, so the stored form
 * and the queried form cannot disagree.
 *
 * Deliberately conservative: case folding and whitespace only.
